newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds up, slightly underperform UK, Germany.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds up, slightly underperform UK, Germany.

text.p: Irish government bonds were marginally up in thin late trade on Friday as the domestic market traded independent of overseas influence, dealers said.
"Basically, the market has traded independent of what has happened overseas," one dealer said. "Dublin has slightly underperformed the UK and Germany, but nothing too dramatic."
By 1555 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 had risen 10 pence to 101.85 to yield 5.96 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 had risen 15 pence to 109.00 to yield 6.60 percent.
Irish September retail sales figures released earlier had little impact on the market, dealers said.
Dealers said a close eye was likely to the kept on the UK over the early part of next week with the spotlight trained on the British budget on Tuesday.
